errors.english: means that if non-existence is absent, then there is existence
errors.why: med na med pa can is the technical 'invariably concomitant' (avinābhāvin): the negation does not occur without [difference], as the commentary immediately explains; it is not a statement that absence of non-existence yields existence.

errors.english: do things not appear to yogis through perception even when they are past and so on?
errors.why: The Tibetan asks how what appears to yogis through perception could still be past etc. (it would be present), the first horn of a dilemma; the English turns it into the opposite question.

note: Follows the argument in outline, but the opening verse's technical concomitance and one horn of the yogic-perception dilemma are misread.

errors.why: ཟེར་རོ ('so they say') closes the previous sentence; གཞན་ནི་ལུང་དུ་མ་བསྟན་པའོ is the root-text lemma 'the other is indeterminate', not 'others say'.

errors.english: In this context, however, they are asserted to be the fruit of (Samadhi) meditative absorption.
errors.why: What is held here to be the fruit of samādhi is the emanation-born virtue under discussion, not the afflicted, karma-born terrifying emanations that 'they' now refers to.

errors.english: It is because they are not substantial entities.
errors.why: dngos po here means the primary/literal sense (the vipāka proper is the vipāka-consciousness) as opposed to a figurative sense (dngos po ma yin pa'i tshul), not 'substantial entity'.

note: Generally readable, but the quoted lemma is turned into a report of others' opinion and the primary/figurative distinction is rendered as substantiality.

errors.english: In the southeast and in the northwest,
errors.why: The Tibetan names the elemental maṇḍalas fire, wind, Mahendra (earth) and water; the English converts them to directions throughout the Sampuṭa verse.

errors.english: And its quarters during the first day and night
errors.why: The figure is three and three-quarters breaths; 'and its quarters' loses the 'three' of the quarters.

note: A competent rendering of the time-reckoning and breathing passage, with the elemental maṇḍalas recast as directions and one figure blurred.
Faithful rendering of the flask and line-drawing ritual, mantras transcribed and glossed accurately.
Faithful, terminologically careful translation of the commentary on names as adventitious.

errors.english: even if the counter-argument — that desire does not occur in those free from it — is not observed
errors.why: mi mthun pa'i phyogs is the dissimilar case (vipakṣa): even though the reason is not seen to occur in the dissimilar case, the passionless, the sign is still inconclusive.

fix.find: even if the counter-argument — that desire does not occur in those free from it — is not observed
fix.replace: even though the reason is not observed to occur in the dissimilar case (vipakṣa), namely those free from desire

errors.english: they lack the power to act upon those who are entirely free from the stubborn attachment to "I" and "mine."
errors.why: Body and faculties by themselves, without grasping at I and mine, have no capacity; the Tibetan is about the causes alone, not about persons free of grasping.

errors.english: because there are other contributing causes that must be considered
errors.why: The other cause to be depended on is the material/substantial cause (upādāna), not merely 'contributing causes'.

note: The inference discussion is followed in outline, but the logical vocabulary (vipakṣa, upādāna) is misrendered at key points.

errors.english: the results produced by self-reproach, full confession, and so forth, are either diminished by some means
errors.why: Self-reproach, confession etc. are the means by which a karma's result is diminished or exhausted, not the producers of the result that gets diminished.

errors.english: If one wonders, "How is it that by the very experience of the result of sinful deeds
errors.why: The lemma 'mixed capacity' (nus 'dres) that this gloss explains is dropped.

note: Readable, but the key statement of the author's own view on confession inverts the roles of means and result.
Faithful rendering of the commentary and embedded sūtra dialogue; supplying Subhūti as speaker is justified by context.

errors.english: **Dha** [note: transliterated as "Da" in the Tibetan OCR but represents the Sanskrit aspirated Dha]
errors.why: ཌ is the retroflex Ḍa of the Arapacana (ḍamara, disturbance), not an aspirated Dha.

fix.find: **Dha** [note: transliterated as "Da" in the Tibetan OCR but represents the Sanskrit aspirated Dha]

errors.english: possessing [note: the qualities of a Buddha]
errors.why: mnga' ba completes the previous side's mi mnga' ba: the Buddha has no loss of the vision of liberation's wisdom; it is not 'possessing the qualities'.

errors.english: because they are disciplined and the locations of discipline are completely severed
errors.why: Both taming and the basis of taming are severed; 'disciplined' is not a separate predicate asserted of phenomena.

note: Sound rendering of the unshared qualities and Arapacana gates, with a wrong note on Ḍa and a misleading boundary note.

errors.english: This is the first section regarding the fifth topic, the elements of the (yoginis).
errors.why: A grammatical note: the first (nominative) case is used in the sense of the fifth (ablative), 'from the elements of the yoginīs'; it is not a section or topic number.

fix.find: This is the first section regarding the fifth topic, the elements of the (yoginis).
fix.replace: The first case is used in the sense of the fifth (ablative): from the elements of the (yoginis).

errors.english: according to the text stating that the primary qualities are all of one nature
errors.why: It cites the root-text line 'the Lord, the nature of all qualities' (gtso bo yon tan kun rang bzhin), not a statement that primary qualities share one nature.

note: The sacred-site lists and the 36x36 computation are right, but quoted root-text lines and a grammatical remark are misread.
